# Concurrent tightening by a common upper cap-volume level

This is an ordinary convex-body reduction for minimal positive circuits. It removes a specific obstruction to extending a three-cap overlap argument: the functional below need not be coordinatewise increasing when r>1. No full-rank stationary-section inequality is assumed or proved here.

## The reduction

Let K be a full-dimensional convex body in R^d, V=vol_d(K), and let u_1,...,u_m be nonzero normals spanning a space of dimension m-1. Suppose their unique linear dependence, up to scale, is

    sum_i rho_i u_i=0,     rho_i>0.

Let H_i={x:u_i.x>=b_i} cover R^d. Write A_i=vol_d(K intersect H_i). Assume initially 0<A_i<V for every i. For any real r<m there exist thresholds b_i'>=b_i such that:

1. All hyperplanes u_i.x=b_i' have a common affine intersection.
2. The new caps H_i' still cover R^d and are subsets of the original caps.
3. With A_i'=vol_d(K intersect H_i'),

       sum_i A_i' - r min_i A_i'
          <= sum_i A_i - r min_i A_i.

4. If the original hyperplanes were not already concurrent, the last inequality is strict.

The statement uses the actual cap volumes and permits oblique normals. There is no arbitrary affine change of a lattice or discrete sum.

## Proof

Let h_i=max_{x in K}u_i.x and l_i=min_{x in K}u_i.x. The cap-volume function

    v_i(b)=vol_d(K intersect {u_i.x>=b})

is continuous and strictly decreasing from V to zero on [l_i,h_i]. Continuity follows by dominated convergence because hyperplanes have d-volume zero. Strict decrease between two interior levels follows because the open slab between them meets int(K) in a nonempty open set. Thus for every s in (0,V) there is a unique continuous inverse threshold Q_i(s) in (l_i,h_i); Q_i(s) tends to h_i as s decreases to zero. The original proper cap has b_i=Q_i(A_i).

The linear map x -> (u_i.x)_i has image exactly the hyperplane {v:sum_i rho_i v_i=0}, by the rank assumption. Consequently the original cover is equivalent to

    sum_i rho_i b_i<=0.

Indeed a point omitted by all closed caps would have u_i.x<b_i for every i, which is impossible if the displayed sum is nonpositive. Conversely, if that sum is positive, take c=(sum_i rho_i b_i)/(sum_i rho_i)>0. The vector (b_i-c)_i lies in the image of the linear map and supplies a point omitted by every cap.

For 0<t<=max_i A_i set

    a_i(t)=min{A_i,t},
    b_i(t)=Q_i(a_i(t)),
    s(t)=sum_i rho_i b_i(t).

These thresholds only increase as t decreases, and are continuous. At t=max_i A_i they are the original thresholds. Moreover

    lim_{t down to 0} s(t)=sum_i rho_i h_i>0.

For the strict inequality, take x_0 in int(K). Every h_i>u_i.x_0, since u_i is nonzero, and the weighted sum of the latter scalar products is zero. Thus the intermediate value theorem supplies t_*>0 with s(t_*)=0. If the initial sum is negative then t_*<max_i A_i. On the interval below max_i A_i, s increases strictly as t decreases, because at least one proper cap mass decreases and every rho_i is positive.

Put b_i'=b_i(t_*). Since their weighted sum is zero, the vector (b_i') lies in the image of the linear map, so the cutting hyperplanes have a common point. Their positive normal dependence makes the new closed caps cover all of R^d. Their cap volumes are exactly a_i(t_*).

It remains to check the functional without asserting coordinatewise monotonicity. Put a=min_i A_i. For t>=a,

    sum_i a_i(t)-r min_i a_i(t)=sum_i min{A_i,t}-r a,

which decreases when any upper cap mass is reduced. For 0<t<=a it equals (m-r)t, which strictly decreases as t decreases because r<m. Hence the functional is nonincreasing throughout the threshold adjustment, and decreases strictly whenever t_*<max_i A_i. This proves all claims.

## Consequence for overlap inequalities

Fix 0<=r<=m-1. Suppose a theorem has been proved for every CONCURRENT proper m-cap cover with this positive-circuit normal pattern:

    sum_i vol_d(K intersect H_i)-V
        >= r min_i vol_d(K intersect H_i).

The same inequality then holds for every possibly nonconcurrent cover with that pattern. Proper caps follow by the preceding reduction. If a cap has zero volume, the desired inequality is just the union bound. If a cap has volume V, the other m-1 cap volumes sum to at least (m-1) times the minimum, which is at least r times the minimum. Thus the extreme cap cases need no quantile inverse.

When all caps are proper and r<m, equality in the transferred inequality forces the original planes to be concurrent. In particular, the coefficient r=m-1/gamma_d proposed for m=d+1 satisfies 0<=r<=m-1 for d>=1, and this reduction applies to it. The genuinely unproved issue remains the concurrent full-rank inequality and its boundary cases. This note does not supply them.
